newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire suspends outspoken army chief.
newsitem.headline: Zaire suspends outspoken army chief.

text.p: Authorities suspended Zaire's outspoken army chief of staff General Eluki Monga on Wednesday for saying a multinational force was no longer needed in Zaire.
"General Eluki has been suspended because of the declarations he made," government spokesman Boguo Makeli said in a statement read after the lunchtime news on state television.
Eluki told French radio on Tuesday that the intervention of a U.N. force in Zaire was now unnecessary after the exodus home of nearly half a million Rwandan refugees.

A government official said Eluki also repeated complaints by the army that the government was not giving the military the means to battle Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels who have seized much of Zaire's two eastern provinces.
The Zaire government maintains that a multinational force is still needed to help hundreds of thousands of other refugees and Zairean villagers displaced by fighting since October 18.

The suspension was announced as Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo and Interior Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda prepared to meet the U.N.'s designated commander for a planned Zairean force, Canadian General Maurice Baril.
The internataional community is divided on whether to still send the force, initially intended to protect more than a million Rwandan refugees trapped by fighting.
The United States has signalled no American combat troops would now be sent to Zaire. U.S. participation would be reduced to humanitarian assistance for returning refugees in Rwanda.
France which spearheaded the idea of intervention maintains the same position as Zaire in favour of foreign troops.
Eluki's renewed attack on the government came as a surprise after the army reversed its earlier criticism of the government and said it was plotting a counter-offensive against rebels.
